name: logger
description: Writes messages into the system log from scripts and the command line.

flags.description: Tag the message with an identifier, e.g. the script name.
Log the contents of a file.
Also echo the message to stderr.

examples.explanation: Writes to the system log, visible in journalctl or /var/log/syslog.
Tagged, prioritized message — filterable later with journalctl -t backup-script.
Captures an entire script's output into the system log — a lightweight job-logging pattern.

about: logger sends messages to syslog/journald via the system socket. It is the correct way for scripts to produce logs that land in the same place as system logs, with proper timestamps, hostnames, and priorities.
useCases: Centralize script output with real timestamps.
mistakes: Logging secrets (tokens, passwords) into the system log — logs are widely readable.
